thesis: The speaker argues that while Ben Graham's framework of buying businesses at a deep discount to their intrinsic value provided strong downside protection, it caused investors to miss the significant upside of holding great compounding machines that grow in value over time. Consequently, the speaker admits that sticking to a strict intrinsic value 'red line' was a mistake and that one should hold robust businesses even when their market price exceeds their intrinsic value by 20%, 30%, or 40%.
